attacks.claim: The QA summary reports results from a staff pilot that the rollout section schedules for Nov 2-6, after today's date of 2026-10-26. Pilot outcomes are presented as completed evidence for a gate happening before that pilot runs.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified" vs. "1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: The public announcement says every cardholder gets text alerts, but the opt-in is unchecked by default and juvenile cards never see it. The text goes out on posters and the e-newsletter, which cannot be recalled, so it misstates the program to the public.
attacks.evidence: "Announcement text says exactly: \"Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder.\"" vs. "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: No retention rule covers phone numbers and consent records for patrons who reply STOP or never confirm after the 72 h purge. Opt-out clears only a flag, so the phone number stays in the patron record indefinitely with no stated end-of-life.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record"; STOP "clears the opt-in flag"; no retention period given for these fields.

attacks.claim: On permanent SMS withdrawal, consent records are deleted within 30 days. That removes the library's proof of patron consent, which is needed to defend any later text-messaging complaint. Legal review LGL-118 covers only the privacy policy text, not this deletion.
attacks.evidence: "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed." vs. "legal review complete (ticket LGL-118)" (policy section 4 only).

attacks.claim: The locker pickup code is sent as plaintext SMS to any phone that replied YES, including a guardian's own number on a linked account. Confirming a phone proves control of the number, not authority over the minor's holds, so a non-custodial or estranged guardian could receive codes for a juvenile cardholder's holds. The code also sits in provider message logs for 30 days.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account"; message body "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14"; "it retains message logs 30 days".

attacks.claim: Message text reveals which branch locker a patron uses and how many holds they have to anyone who sees the phone's lock screen. Titles are excluded, which limits the exposure.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker."

attacks.claim: SMS delivery depends on one provider, and the spend-cap fallback relies on a separate automated phone-call channel whose vendor and exit path are not named.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA"; fallback to "automated phone call, which stays on file"

attacks.claim: All texts queued overnight release at 08:00 at once, creating a burst. The artifact does not check whether 10DLC throughput limits or the provider rate limits can absorb that spike for a 210k-cardholder base.
On spend-cap trigger, all opted-in patrons fall back to automated phone calls, but those calls are not in the $460/month forecast or the BM-26-14 budget, and their cost is not capped.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call"

attacks.claim: Five wrong codes lock a locker cell and alert staff, but the artifact has no runbook or staff unlock procedure, so a patron could be stuck at a locker until someone responds.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff."

attacks.claim: When locker_pickup is turned off, codes already sent by text are not said to be invalidated or honored, so a patron could try an old code at a locker that is being emptied.
attacks.evidence: "holds currently assigned to a locker ... are remapped to the branch desk"; no statement on previously sent codes.

attacks.claim: Batching extra holds into one text is specified, but the message template names one locker. The artifact does not say what the batched text shows when holds sit at different pickup locations.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message" vs. "2 holds ready at Oak St locker"

attacks.claim: Accessibility testing covers only the opt-in web form. The locker touchscreen, audio-guidance headphone path, and card reader have no screen-reader or low-vision test in the QA table. The service desk fallback mitigates this.
attacks.evidence: QA row "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS" only; "audio guidance through a headphone jack"; "Holds stay collectible at the service desk".

attacks.claim: No attack under this lens. The message copy and opt-in disclosure are rendered and tested at three viewport widths.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no rendering defect identified in the artifact text.

attacks.claim: No attack under this lens. The feature addresses a stated patron need for notification and off-hours pickup.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no value mismatch identified in the artifact text.

attacks.claim: No attack under this lens. The opt-in flow is short and the service desk remains available.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no added step or latency issue identified in the artifact text.

attacks.claim: No attack under this lens. Flags, rollback steps, and the remap script are documented.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no hidden coupling or scope drift identified in the artifact text.
